newsitem.title: USA: Orange County bankruptcy trial delayed - court.
newsitem.headline: Orange County bankruptcy trial delayed - court.

text.p: Defense arguments in the trial of Orange County, Calif.,'s former assistant treasurer, Matthew Raabe, were delayed until April 21, court officials said on Monday.
Raabe's defense team was expected to begin presenting its case early Monday but agreed at a court hearing in Santa Ana to the one week delay, which was requested by county prosecutors.

The prosecution, which has already rested its case, alleged that Raabe helped to divert nearly $90 million in interest earnings owed to cities, schools and special districts that invested in the county-run portfolio.
Last week, Superior Court Judge Everett Dickey rejected a defense motion seeking dismissal of the bankruptcy-related charges against Raabe.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments.
The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Raabe, who faces up to 12 years in prison, was one of several Orange County officials to face charges following the bankruptcy. His trial was expected to last into May.
In April 1995, former Orange County Treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to six felonies for his role in the crisis.
A judge last November ordered him to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine, but Citron was later assigned to a community work program instead of jail.
Citron claimed that Raabe was the "mastermind" behind the scheme to divert the interest earnings.
Last October, a judge sentenced former Orange County budget director Ronald Rubino to probation for charges stemming from the investment crisis.
